drug_class: Bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) antibody / cancer immunotherapy
purpose: Blinatumomab is used to treat a type of blood cancer called acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), specifically when it involves B-cells. It is used in adults and children whose cancer has come back or has not responded to other treatments. It can also be used to treat a condition where leukemia cells are still detectable in the blood even when the patient seems to be in remission.
how_it_works: Think of this medicine as a connector or bridge. It grabs onto two things at once — a cancer cell on one end and one of your own immune cells (called a T-cell) on the other end. By bringing them together, it helps your immune system recognize and destroy the leukemia cells. Basically, it trains your body's own defense system to fight the cancer.
common_side_effects: Fever, chills, and flu-like symptoms (very common, especially at the start), headache, nausea, low blood counts (which can increase infection or bleeding risk), fatigue, swelling, and low potassium or other electrolyte changes in the blood.
warnings: This medication has two very important serious risks. First, it can cause a dangerous reaction called Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), where your immune system overreacts — signs include high fever, low blood pressure, and breathing problems. Second, it can affect the brain and nervous system, causing confusion, seizures, or trouble speaking. Because of these risks, you will be watched closely, especially when starting the medicine or increasing the dose. It is given in a hospital setting or with close medical supervision. It also comes with a boxed warning — the FDA's strongest warning — for these serious neurological and CRS risks.
typical_dosing: Blinatumomab is given as a continuous IV infusion, meaning it drips slowly into your vein non-stop over several days or weeks through a small pump. A typical treatment cycle lasts about 4 weeks of continuous infusion followed by a 2-week break. Your doctor will decide how many cycles you need based on how your body responds. Dosing is based on your body weight and adjusted for children.
